newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Moroccan rights group says local poll was flawed.
newsitem.headline: Moroccan rights group says local poll was flawed.

text.p: Morocco's independent Human Rights Associations (AMDH) on Thursday denounced what it described as "irregularities and human rights abuse" during communal elections of June 13.

Abderrahmane Benameur, head of AMDH, told a news conference "the administration was not neutral at all before and during local elections of June 13...In some areas local authorities were involved in the manipulation of results".
Interior Minister Driss Basri told a news conference last Saturday that the administration "did not untervene at any stage in the local election process".

Benameur cited as one example the case of Sidi Bettach constituency near Rabat where he said a former political detainee won a seat "but local authorities intervened violently to change the final result".

He named the detainee as Abdallah Agaou, a former military officer who spent 18 years in the remote Atlas mountain Tazmamart secret jail after he was accused of involvement in a military coup attempt against the monarchy in the early 1970s.
The AMDH said preliminary results showed that communal and municipal seats "were divided into three blocs to respond exactly to the authorities' will".

Preliminary results released by the interior ministry showed that pro-government and centre-right parties dominated the elections, with the opposition four-party Koutla bloc winning 7,532 seats out of a total 24,253.

The elections were contested by a dozen parties, most of them linked in three alliances -- opposition Koutla, the pro-government rightist Wifaq group and a centre-right group led by the Independent National Rally.
The local elections for 1,547 councils were the first of a series due to culminate in September with a general election for a new lower house of parliament.

Under the constitution, a new Upper House is to be formed with power to topple the government through a no-confidence motion. Sixty percent of its members will be chosen by the local councils emerging from last week ballot.
AMDH also denouced the arrest of 125 activists of the opposition Avant-Garde Democratic and Socialist Party (PADS) who called for a boycott of local elections earlier this month.
The rights group also said it had reports of some political violence in provinces such as Kelaat Seraghna, near the southern city of Marrakesh and Meknes, in central Morocco.
"We were informed that three people at least were killed during the election process and we are checking the case of three others," an AMDH spokesman said.

An interior ministry official told Reuters a total of "four people were killed in violent disputes between candidates' suporters during the elections...To be clear, the administration has nothing to do with these cases."
